question.text: SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations aim to:

answer.text: Allow selected persons to trade on unpublished price-sensitive information
Prohibit trading based on unpublished price-sensitive information (UPSI) and ensure fair market access to information
Encourage insider trading for market liquidity
Regulate only foreign investors' trading activity

explanation.text: The Logic: Per NISM Series XV pages 261-264, the PIT Regulations define UPSI and prohibit insiders from communicating or providing UPSI except for legitimate purposes (page 263). Page 263 also bars insiders from trading in listed securities while in possession of UPSI. Page 264 supports fair-disclosure obligations, required disclosures and the code-of-conduct controls that insiders and listed entities must implement. The Trap: Insider trading is prohibited, not allowed or encouraged. The regulations apply to all insiders, not just foreign investors. Note: Typical UPSI examples include unpublished financial results, dividends, changes in capital structure, mergers and acquisitions, and changes in key management — until they are made generally available.
